If something lacks the quality of goodness, does that make it bad?

This is one of the concepts explored in the Parsha this week, in which the city of Sodom is destroyed after Abraham is unable to find a single good man within the walls.

God listened patiently to Abraham as he made the case — if I can find just one good man within the walls, you must spare the city.

Sodom itself as it turned out lacked any amount of goodness, allowing God to condemn them as evil. But imagine a world in which Abraham found a good man — just one beacon of light within a sea of evil would have turned the city from an outright bad place to something more nuanced.

This is something to remember, both in life and trading. You need to look for the good contained within the bad — you often we’ll find a more beautiful world.

Shabbat Shalom, I hope everyone has a wonderful and peaceful weekend

#Uranium producers need contracts that make mines worth building.

A margin over reported cash costs is NOT the same as an adequate return on the full investment.

Exploration. Permitting. Mine construction. Processing infrastructure. Labour and energy. Sustaining capital. Financing. Closure.

Plus a return that justifies years of capital at risk.

Headline production costs capture only part of that equation. Producers should demand contract prices and terms that support the entire investment.

For investors, scale matters. Smaller standalone mines can carry substantial infrastructure, regulatory and corporate costs spread across relatively few pounds. Those burdens do not shrink neatly with the deposit.

Larger operations with long mine lives can spread investment and fixed costs across more production.

My preference: scale, longevity and margins that can survive a difficult cycle.

Size alone guarantees nothing. Grade, recovery, mining method and existing infrastructure can make smaller projects competitive. But a small mine with a large funding requirement deserves serious scrutiny.

The price that keeps an existing mine running is not necessarily the price that gets the next one built. New mines need uranium >$200 (at least most mines, a few tier-1 mines might do with a bit less). That is now. Inflation-adjusted it will be much more when the mine is built in 10-20 years.

The highest level of intelligence one can attain is the depth of their self awareness

By definition you cannot make the best decisions for yourself if you arent internally/externally consistent with who you are

This is what gets you intro wrong jobs, wrong relationships, wrong investments etc

For eg If you are not aware that you cant deal with volatility in investing you end up puking when price goes down

You have to know your strengths and weaknesses upfront for any endeavour and then improve on your strengths and cover your weaknesses

A few examples of ways to work on these across different areas:

Personal - Think about and find things that trigger you, those things trigger us because there is something there we havent internally resolved. Getting angry or upset is normal but it simmering for long periods means its not just that ie if someone cutting you in line triggers you its not that they cut the line - it could be that the act makes you feel invisible and worthless as a person

Relationships - Imagine actually being the other person not just empathy. For guys for eg you want an attractive partner for example who is fit etc but why would such a person be attracted to you if you dont have that same focus on yourself? What right do you have to demand that they see you for your personality when you dont?

Investing - Start from view you could be wrong in order to see how you feel about things moving against you

Once you become more consistent in thoughts and actions - every tweak and improvement changes your whole life because you are correctly resolving each situation - when its inconsistent you only get worse 

For eg imagine not knowing that you are a selfish person thinking you are a good person- you will be selfish in relationships and then when it ends you blame the other person as you are just a kind person. 
Everyone including you and me when speaking about past relationships will generally talk about the issues of the other person and conveniently think not much is wrong with them - you just have to acknowledge that you do it and in acknowledging it you will improve

We all have many flaws but being able to label them and accept them goes a long way

Politicians play the game they are dealt just as a sales rep does with phone call metrics

So lastly I would say to try stay consistent with the way you talk and measure things in general - if you dont believe in something dont talk using the things you dont believe in

Be the change you seek
